extracted.intended_audience: Users/developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians and computer-algebra researchers) who need library procedure reference and examples
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for multiple SINGULAR libraries (ncfrac.lib, ncloc.lib, nets.lib, nfmodstd.lib, nfmodsyz.lib, olga.lib) describing procedure usage, purpose, returns, assumptions, and examples. Intended to guide users in calling and understanding library functions and data types.

rubrics_metrics.name: isInvertibleNcfrac
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isInvertibleNcfrac(frac), ncfrac frac. Purpose: checks if frac is invertible. Return: int, 1 if frac is invertible, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show constructing ncfrac values and calling isInvertibleNcfrac to get 1 (invertible) or 0 (not invertible).

rubrics_metrics.name: invertNcfrac
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invertNcfrac(frac), ncfrac frac. Purpose: compute the inverse of frac. Return: ncfrac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: returns the zero fraction if frac is not invertible. Example demonstrates inverting an invertible ncfrac producing the inverse and calling invertNcfrac on a non-invertible fraction returns a zero-like representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: testNcfrac
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: testNcfrac(). Purpose: execute a series of internal testing procedures. Return: nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided as an internal test harness for the ncfrac.lib procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: testNcfracExamples
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: testNcfracExamples(). Purpose: execute the examples of all procedures in this library. Return: nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runs the documented examples for the ncfrac library to demonstrate behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncloc type and operations (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library: ncloc.lib. Purpose: Ore-localization in G-Algebras. Introduces a new type: ncloc. An element of type ncloc has two members: int locType and def locData. Operations: string(ncloc), print(ncloc), status(ncloc), test(ncloc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infix operations: ncloc == ncloc, ncloc != ncloc; constructions: ncloc = list/poly (monoidal localization), ncloc = ideal (geometric localization), ncloc = intvec (rational localization). The overview explains representation choices and available high-level operations for inspection and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: isDenom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isDenom(p, loc), poly p, ncloc loc. Purpose: check if p is a valid denominator in the localization loc. Return: int (1 or 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show monoidal, geometric, and rational localizations with sample polys and indicate when isDenom returns 1 (valid denominator) or 0 (not valid).

rubrics_metrics.name: testNcloc
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: testNcloc(). Purpose: execute a series of internal testing procedures for ncloc.lib. Return: nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to validate internal correctness of ncloc operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: testNclocExamples
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: testNclocExamples(). Purpose: execute the examples of all procedures in this library. Return: nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runs documented examples demonstrating ncloc.lib functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nets overview (pretty printing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nets are arrays of characters printed in matrix format for pretty printing; they can be concatenated horizontally and vertically and any Singular type can be converted to a Net by applying net. Return: visual/character-array representations of objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When concatenating horizontally, empty rows are filled with spaces; conversion routines support many Singular types (poly, matrix, ideal, map, etc.). The library is for producing on-screen visual presentations of objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: catNets
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: catNets(N,M); N,M Nets. Return: horizontal concatenation of N and M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: concatenated horizontally with alignment at the top row. Alias: can be called with '+'. Examples show net('aaa') + net('b') -> 'aaab'.

rubrics_metrics.name: net (conversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: net(X) where X is a Singular object. Purpose: convert a Singular object into a Net (character array) for on-screen printing. Return: Net.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple specialized net* routines exist for different object types; net is the generic conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: netBigIntMat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netBigIntMat(M); M bigint Matrix. Assume: M is a bigintmatrix. Return: visual presentation of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows a 2x2 bigint matrix printed in a boxed row format. Designed for readable display of large integer entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: netBigIntMatShort
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netBigIntMatShort(M); M bigint matrix. Assume: M is a bigintmatrix. Return: visual presentation of M, only the first digits of each entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for abbreviated display of very large integers in matrices; examples demonstrate truncated digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: netCoefficientRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netCoefficientRing(R); R ring. Assume: R is a ring. Return: visual presentation of the coefficient ring of R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converts the ring's coefficient structure into a Net for display (e.g., QQ, FF_p, extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: netIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netIdeal(P); P ideal. Assume: P is an ideal. Return: visual presentation of I as a Net.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays ideals in a compact, readable form; examples show simplification of generators when printed via netIdeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: netInt
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netInt(M); M integer. Assume: M is an integer. Return: visual presentation of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple visual conversion for integer scalars.

rubrics_metrics.name: netBigInt
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netBigInt(M); M bigint. Assume: M is a bigint. Return: visual presentation of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like netInt but for bigints; prints large integers in a Net.

rubrics_metrics.name: netIntMat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netIntMat(M); M int matrix. Assume: M is an int matrix. Return: visual presentation of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printed as a compact matrix block; example shows a 2x2 int matrix output.

rubrics_metrics.name: netIntMatShort
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netIntMatShort(M); M int matrix. Assume: M is an int matrix. Return: visual presentation of M, only the first digits of each entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameter to specify how many leading digits to show (example: netIntMatShort(M,2) gives '11...').

rubrics_metrics.name: netIntVector
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netIntVector(V); V int vector. Assume: V is an int vector. Return: visual presentation of V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays integer vectors as vertically stacked entries in a Net (one per row).

rubrics_metrics.name: netIntVectorShort
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netIntVectorShort(V); V int vector. Assume: V is an int vector. Return: visual presentation of V, only the first digits of each entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts a second argument controlling digit truncation (example netIntVectorShort(V,4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: netNumber
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netNumber(a); a number. Return: visual presentation of a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converts scalar numbers into Nets; example shows '5' printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: netList
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netList(L); L list. Assume: L is a list of elements. Return: visual presentation of L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays lists as bracketed lists; example shows netList([111, x+y, x3y-z, y+3z4]) -> [111, x+y, x3y-z, y+3z4].

rubrics_metrics.name: netMap
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netMap(f); f map. Assume: f is a map from a ring to the basering. Return: visual presentation of the map f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays mapping information (source->target and variable images) in a user-friendly Net. Example shows multi-line mapping output.

rubrics_metrics.name: netMap2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netMap2(f); f map. Assume: f is a map from a ring to the basering. Return: visual presentation of the map f, alternative version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a compact one-line mapping representation; example: 'f: r1 --> r2 , x -> ab , y -> ac , z -> bc'.

rubrics_metrics.name: netmatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netmatrix(M); M matrix. Assume: M is a matrix. Return: visual presentation of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converts polynomial matrices to Nets displayed in rows/columns; examples handle varying polynomial widths and multi-row presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: netmatrixShort
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netmatrixShort(M, width); M matrix. Assume: M is a matrix. Return: visual presentation of M with each entry shortened to width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for displaying matrices with wide polynomial entries truncated to a column width; example uses netmatrixShort(M, 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: netPoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netPoly(P); P poly. Assume: P is a polynomial. Return: visual presentation of P over two rows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays polynomials in a two-row Net format for readability; many examples illustrate behavior across rings and polynomial forms including multivariate and coefficient rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: netPrimePower
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netPrimePower(n,m); n,m int. Return: visual presentation of the prime power n^m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple helper to display prime powers as a Net (e.g., '2^5').

rubrics_metrics.name: netRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netRing(R); R ring. Assume: R is a ring. Return: visual presentation of R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows ring declarations and coefficient field/extension information (examples show FF_32003[x,y,z], QQ[a]/(poly)[x,y,z], etc.). Handles many ring flavors and prints substituted/normalized forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: netString
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netString(M); M string. Assume: M is a string. Return: visual presentation of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converts strings to a Net for printing; example prints 'Hallo'.

rubrics_metrics.name: netvector
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netvector(V); V vector. Assume: V is a vector. Return: visual presentation of V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays general vectors (polynomial entries) as vertical Net columns; example shows polynomial entries stacked.

rubrics_metrics.name: netvectorShort
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: netvectorShort(V); V vector. Assume: V is a vector. Return: visual presentation of V, short version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truncates entries for compact display; examples show combinations of long and truncated polynomial/vector entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: stackNets
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: stackNets(N,M); N,M Nets. Return: vertical concatenation of N and M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: nets concatenated vertically with alignment at the left column. Example shows 'aaa' stacked with 'b' producing two lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: chinrempoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chinrempoly(l, m); l list, m list. Return: a polynomial (resp. ideal/module) congruent to l[i] modulo m[i] for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies Chinese remaindering to list l with moduli m. Requirements: elements in first list must be of the same type (polynomial, ideal, or module); moduli must be polynomials; elements in second list must be distinct and co-prime. Examples show use over finite fields and rationals and also module-version examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfmodStd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: nfmodStd(I, #); I ideal or module, optional # parameters. Return: standard basis of I over algebraic number field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ground field has no parameter, the procedure forwards to modStd (Section D.4.13.1) and passes optional parameters through. Examples demonstrate computing standard bases in algebraic number fields and modules, and handling rings with/without parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfmodSyz
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: nfmodSyz(I); I ideal or module. Return: syzygy module of I over an algebraic number field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes syzygy modules using modular methods and Chinese remaindering; examples include rings with and without parameters and show returned syzygy generators. References and algorithmic overview are provided in the library overview.

rubrics_metrics.name: olga library overview (localization types & fraction rep)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library: olga.lib. Purpose: Ore-localization in G-Algebras. Current localization types: Type 0 (monoidal) represented by list of polys in a commutative polynomial subring; Type 1 (geometric) for algebras with even number of variables where first half induces a commutative polynomial subring, represented by a prime ideal in that subring; Type 2 (rational) represented by an intvec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localization data consists of an int specifying type and a def with corresponding information. Fractions represented as vector [s,r,p,t] with s^{-1}r (left) and pt^{-1} (right); s or t zero means representation unset; both zero -> invalid fraction. Reference to a paper provided for full constructive theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: locStatus (validation rules for localization data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: locStatus(locType, locData), int locType, list/vector/intvec locData. Purpose: determine the status of a set of localization data. Return: list where first entry is 0/1 (valid/invalid) and second entry is a string with a status/error message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation rules and error messages shown in examples: invalid type values rejected; uninitialized/undefined locData rejected; for monoidal (type 0) locData must be a non-empty list of polynomials/ints/numbers whose variables induce a commutative polynomial subring; for geometric (type 1) the basering must have even number of variables and first half must induce a commutative polynomial subring, locData must be an ideal generated by polynomials using only variables from the first half; for rational (type 2) locData must be intvec in correct range. Examples demonstrate specific failure messages for mismatched types and contents.
